problem: EQA methods that couple navigation with QA perform poorly (sometimes worse than question-only baselines), so it is unclear whether the bottleneck is navigation or visual reasoning. EQA-v1 also has only 4 simple single-object question types.
motivation: Decoupling reasoning from navigation, by giving the agent near-ideal trajectories, lets one test whether VQA-style methods can handle rich egocentric videos and complex questions. This gives a feasibility estimate for EQA and a benchmark for progress before navigation is reintroduced.
key_idea: Build VideoNavQA, a synthetic dataset of shortest-path House3D videos paired with template-generated existence, counting, comparison and query questions, and benchmark adapted VQA and video models on it.
insight: Every video-based model beats the language-only LSTM (56.49%) and BoW (49.02%), so the videos are informative and models exploit visual context. Overall accuracies are tightly clustered (62.3-64.5%) across very different architectures, so architecture matters little and better video reasoning is needed. Per-category results differ: MAC is best on counting, color and room location, while Concat-CNN2D is best on count comparison. Video-only models reach only 33% (predicting the majority answer).
method: Dataset generation: shortest-path trajectories between rooms in House3D (SUNCG), rendered as videos; ground truth extracted via semantic and depth rendering of visible objects and rooms.

Question generation: 28 templates in 8 categories with 70 possible answers, instantiated from ground-truth tag sets and validated by executing functional programs (filter/count/unique/get_attr). About 101k video-question pairs split by house: 622/65/56 houses for train/val/test.
Baselines: LSTM and BoW question-only models, plus video-only V-CNN2D (VGG+LSTM) and V-CNN3D (C3D-like).
Concat models: Concat-CNN2D/3D concatenate the LSTM question embedding with the video representation, then apply an MLP and softmax.
Per-frame FiLM: ResBlocks conditioned by question-derived FiLM parameters, applied to each frame, then aggregated by recurrent attention (FiLM-AT) or global max-pooling (FiLM-GP).
Temporal multi-hop FiLM: FiLM parameters at frame t come from attention over question hidden states, with the context initialized from frame t-1; temporal summarization by max-pooling.
MAC: a MAC cell applied on 2D-CNN features and integrated over time by an LSTM.
Feature and sampling tricks: features from a Faster R-CNN-initialized detector pre-trained on 2000 extra frames; random sub-sampling of 1 of every 4 frames cuts length from 140 to 35.

setting.backbone: Small CNN/LSTM/FiLM/MAC models trained from scratch (LSTM question encoder + CNN2D/3D video encoders; FiLM, multi-hop FiLM, MAC)
setting.training_data: VideoNavQA train split: 84,990 question-video pairs from 622 SUNCG houses; small object detector pre-trained on 2000 extra frames
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB video (140 frames of 3x160x208) along a shortest-path trajectory, plus a text question
setting.action_space: none (question answering over a given video; classification over 70 answers)
setting.privileged: Near-optimal shortest-path trajectory is provided so the video contains the answer information; ground truth is used only for dataset generation.

numbers.extra: Faster R-CNN-initialized pre-trained features; random frame sub-sampling

numbers_note: Only the new VideoNavQA benchmark is evaluated. Per-category accuracies appear only in a figure. Other rows: Concat-CNN3D 64.00, FiLM-GP 63.79, LSTM 56.49, BoW 49.02, V-CNN3D 33.29, V-CNN2D 33.62.
results: Concat-CNN2D is best at 64.47% test accuracy, with Concat-CNN3D 64.00, FiLM-AT 64.08, FiLM-GP 63.79, temporal multi-hop 63.53 and MAC 62.32. All beat the LSTM-only baseline (56.49%), and the video-only models sit at about 33%. Task difficulty remains high even with near-ideal navigation.
limitations: Synthetic template questions and shortest-path videos in House3D/SUNCG; the setting is not the real EQA loop (no navigation, no agent-in-the-loop) and may not transfer.
Models give only modest gains over the language-only baseline (about 8 points) and are very similar to each other; no human-performance reference is given.
Videos are subsampled and features are pre-extracted, limiting the capacity of reasoning models (about 5 h/epoch training).
